title: Manitoba Issues 53 Immigration Invitations to Skilled Workers in Targeted Recruitment Draw
excerpt: The province's August 13 draw focused on candidates directly recruited through employer, francophone, ethnocultural, and regional community initiatives.
body:
• Manitoba issued 53 Letters of Advice to Apply on August 13, targeting skilled workers recruited through the province's strategic recruitment initiatives.
  • Invitations were distributed across five initiative categories: Employer Services (15), Francophone Community (13), Ethnocultural Communities (12), Regional Communities (9), and the Temporary Public Policy stream (4).
  • Manitoba has allotted 6,239 provincial nomination spaces for 2026 and has issued 2,670 nominations through the first half of the year.
  • Six of the 53 invitees had valid Express Entry profiles, potentially fast-tracking their permanent residency applications.

August 13 Draw Details

The Manitoba Provincial Nominee Program issued 53 Letters of Advice to Apply on August 13 through both pathways of its Skilled Worker Stream — candidates already in Manitoba and those overseas. This was the province's 16th draw of 2026, according to CIC News.

https://x.com/canadavisa_com/status/2089306661030871530

Unlike Manitoba's larger general draws — which have recently topped 2,000 invitations — this round specifically targeted candidates who had been directly invited by the MPNP under a strategic recruitment initiative. To qualify, candidates needed to specify in their Expression of Interest profile that they had received a direct invitation through a recruitment mission or the now-expired Temporary Public Policy to Facilitate Work Permits for Prospective Provincial Nominee Candidates.

How Invitations Were Distributed

Candidates recruited through the Employer Services initiative received the largest share, accounting for 15 of the 53 LAAs, or 28.3% of the total. The Francophone Community pathway issued 13 invitations, followed by Ethnocultural Communities with 12 and Regional Communities with 9. Four LAAs went to candidates under the Temporary Public Policy stream.

Six of the invited candidates had declared valid Express Entry profile numbers and job seeker validation codes in their EOI. For these applicants, a successful provincial nomination feeds directly into the federal Express Entry system, substantially improving their Comprehensive Ranking System score and accelerating the path to permanent residency.

Manitoba's 2026 Immigration Pace

Manitoba has been allotted 6,239 provincial nomination spaces by the federal government for 2026. Through the first six months of the year, the province issued 2,670 nominations, with 886 of those classified as enhanced nominations. Monthly nomination volumes have been steady, ranging from 389 in March to 505 in June.

The total number of LAAs issued through the Skilled Worker Stream since the program's inception stands at 4,875. Application volumes have picked up sharply, with 554 received in May and 589 in June, compared to just 104 in March.

Common Pitfalls for Applicants

Manitoba noted that some candidates who appeared to meet draw requirements did not receive invitations due to profile errors. The most frequent disqualifiers include expired or invalid language test identification numbers and failure to provide valid strategic recruitment initiative invitation numbers. Candidates who claim eligibility under a recruitment initiative without entering a verified MPNP invitation code are automatically excluded from selection.

What It Means for Indian Workers

Manitoba's provincial nominee program has been a significant pathway for Indian immigrants to Canada. The Ethnocultural Communities recruitment stream, which issued 12 of the 53 LAAs in this draw, is particularly relevant for diaspora communities seeking to establish roots in the province. Manitoba's relatively lower cost of living compared to Toronto and Vancouver, combined with strong demand for skilled workers in manufacturing, transportation, and healthcare, has made it an increasingly popular destination for Indian professionals.

What's Next

With more than half of the year's nomination allocation still available, Manitoba is expected to continue holding regular draws through the fall. Recent draws have varied significantly in size — from 53 targeted invitations in this round to over 2,100 in a July 16 draw that included international student graduates and francophone candidates. Prospective applicants should ensure their EOI profiles have current language test results and accurate recruitment initiative details to avoid disqualification.
